video.title: Stop Chasing Billion Dollar Ideas. Do This Instead.

summary: Chris Koerner and an unnamed guest discuss small, testable business ideas, including a cooking app, social media theme pages, digital guides and AI-generated business plans. Chris describes a programmatic workflow for repurposing viral cooking videos and says he tests offers with paid ads. The guest explains Unlimited Content’s SEO blog service and how it uses AI with human editing. Their shared theme is to make a clear offer, test it quickly and sell convenience while keeping delivery simple.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: The Koerner Office host; also referred to as Chris in the transcript.

speakers.name: Guest (name not stated)
speakers.description: Discusses Unlimited Content and its SEO content service.

ideas.name: Unlimited Content SEO blog service
ideas.one_liner: A monthly service that writes and publishes SEO blog content for businesses using AI and human editing.
ideas.customer: Businesses that want regular SEO blog content but do not want to handle the tools, editing, publishing and image curation themselves.
ideas.problem: Customers know they need regular blog content to compete in search, but creating and publishing it takes time and requires learning tools and processes.
ideas.offer: Daily blog posts produced with AI and a human editor, with editing, publishing and image curation handled for the customer.

pricing.notes: The guest compares the service's price with spending the same amount on tools and doing the work independently.

acquisition_channels.details: The guest says they take sales calls and have around 40 leads a week to close; the transcript does not explain how the calls or leads are sourced.

quote.text: we have 40 leads of week that like need to be closed for this other thing
quote.speaker: Guest (name not stated)

ideas.delivery: The service produces daily blog posts using AI and a human editor. The guest describes onboarding clients, exporting their website, collecting existing SEO data from Search Atlas or Semrush, and using ChatGPT to produce an SEO content strategy. The team handles editing, publishing and image curation.
unit_economics_claims: The guest says the service costs $400 per month and compares that with the time and tools a customer would need to do the work themselves.

acquisition.how: Sales calls and lead closing are human-led in the transcript. Software can help identify and qualify business leads, but contact must follow UK marketing rules.

onboarding.how: Automate website exports and SEO data collection, then use a structured prompt to draft each client's content strategy; a person should check the inputs and plan.

delivery.how: AI drafts content, but the guest explicitly describes a human editor and team work on editing, publishing and image curation.

billing.how: A monthly retainer can be billed through recurring payments with routine human checks; the transcript does not state the billing system.

support.how: The offer reduces customer workload, but sales calls and ongoing client needs imply human account management.

uk_applicability.notes: SEO content services can be sold to UK businesses. The service would need to follow UK data protection and marketing rules when sourcing and contacting leads.

risks: The guest says prospective customers may believe they can do the work themselves, so the offer needs to explain the time and operational effort it removes.
Daily AI-assisted content still needs human review for accuracy, originality and usefulness.
The transcript does not provide retention, delivery-cost or margin data.

pricing.notes: The speakers also joke about offering a discount, doubling the price and applying a 50% first-month promotion; these are not presented as settled pricing.

acquisition_channels.details: The plan is to test Facebook ads, sending traffic both to a landing page and directly to the App Store, then compare the results.

unit_economics_claims: The speaker gives an annual subscription price of $60.
The speaker speculates the app could make $100,000 to $200,000, but says they do not expect to build a career from it.

ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; the app was awaiting payment integration completion and App Store submission.

acquisition.how: Paid ads and social content can be scheduled and optimized with software, but creative decisions, ad review and budget approval need human oversight.

onboarding.how: An app subscription can use an automated signup and payment flow; the transcript does not describe onboarding.

delivery.how: Software can deliver app functionality automatically once built, though the transcript does not explain the AI features or human review.

billing.how: Stripe and App Store billing can support recurring subscriptions, subject to payment integration and exception handling.

support.how: App support could be handled with automated help and escalation, but no support process is stated.

uk_applicability.notes: A cooking app distributed through app stores can serve UK users. Localize any food, nutrition or allergen guidance and comply with UK consumer and privacy rules.

risks: The app had not yet completed payment integration or App Store review, so release and revenue timing were uncertain.
The speaker plans to test paid acquisition but gives no cost-per-install, conversion or retention data.
AI cooking advice may be inaccurate or unsafe if it gives poor food handling or allergen guidance.

ideas.name: Repurposed viral social media theme pages
ideas.one_liner: Build niche social accounts by finding viral videos, adding a recurring caption and scheduling batches of posts.
ideas.business_model: Not stated; the transcript describes audience building and content production, but not a clear revenue model.
ideas.customer: Not stated; the immediate audience is people interested in a niche such as vegan recipes, music discovery or business ideas.
ideas.offer: Niche social video feeds that add a persistent caption to third-party videos, such as a series about finding viral vegan recipes.

pricing.notes: The transcript does not state how the theme pages themselves earn money.

acquisition_channels.details: Search Instagram on a desktop browser for a niche hashtag, select promising viral videos, add links to a spreadsheet and publish them with a recurring caption. The speaker describes this for Instagram and says similar content is used across social platforms.

quote.text: all I do is I just scroll on that account for like 10 minutes grab 60 videos
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: The transcript discusses reposting and transforming video content on YouTube, while also describing copyright strikes as a platform risk.

quote.text: YouTube is very strict about it Facebook is strict about it Instagram is not strict about it Tik Tok is not strict about it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: The creator selects videos, adds a recurring top caption and sometimes gives creator credit. Zapier, a spreadsheet, Apify, Airtable, Bannerbear, Dropbox and Hopper HQ are used to collect, format and schedule posts. A person still selects source videos and bulk uploads the finished content.
unit_economics_claims: The speaker says the batch workflow takes about 45 minutes and produces a month's worth of content.
The speaker says the recurring caption format produces a threefold to sixfold increase in view-to-follow conversion.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; the described workflow uses several named services, but their costs are not given.

acquisition.how: A person still selects source posts, but software can collect links, generate templates and schedule publishing. Reposting or messaging creators without permission creates legal and platform risks.

onboarding.how: Once a theme and template are configured, a new batch can be added through a spreadsheet workflow; a person must choose the account's niche and settings.

delivery.how: Software automates caption overlays, file routing and scheduling, but a person selects content and checks rights, credits and output quality.

billing.how: No revenue or billing system is described.

support.how: Comments and creator requests can be triaged with tools, but copyright complaints and audience moderation need human decisions.

uk_applicability.notes: The workflow can be run in the UK, but platform rules, copyright and data protection still apply. The speaker's assertion that a repost is fair use is not a reliable UK legal basis.

risks: The speaker reports receiving YouTube copyright strikes and says three strikes in 60 days can delete an account.
Adding captions or context does not automatically grant permission to reuse someone else's video; fair dealing rules in the UK differ from US fair use.
Accounts can lose reach or be removed if platforms change their policies or detect reused content.
The speaker says they sometimes credit creators, but does not describe a permission process.

ideas.name: General store for digital guides
ideas.one_liner: A branded online store that sells multiple low-ticket how-to guides across different niches.
ideas.business_model: One-off digital product sales, potentially with repeat purchases across related niches.
ideas.customer: People searching for practical how-to information, such as cooking, fitness or personal finance guides.
ideas.problem: Customers want useful information about a specific task or interest and may prefer a paid, ready-to-use guide to a free lead magnet.
ideas.offer: A branded catalogue of digital guides such as cookbooks, a guide to improving mile time, pizza or sourdough guides, and personal finance spreadsheets.

pricing.model: One-off guide sales at low ticket prices, with product and price testing.

price_points.label: Example upper price in the discussed range
High-ticket course comparison, not the proposed guide price

pricing.notes: The speakers discuss testing price points from $17 to $99 and potentially higher. They contrast guides under $100 with a $5,000 course.

acquisition_channels.details: Run Facebook ads to individual products and test niches, offers, positioning and prices from one Shopify store.

quote.text: you can test 15 different niches different offers different positionings overnight out of a single Shopify store
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Use Etsy listings and sales data to identify what digital products people are searching for and buying.

quote.text: you can go get digital products on Etsy people are searching for them
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Create digital guides, list them in Shopify and deliver them online after purchase. AI is proposed for creating content and ads. No specific delivery platform or quality-control process is stated.
unit_economics_claims: The speakers argue that digital products avoid physical inventory and fulfillment costs and can have a simpler cost structure of revenue minus marketing.
A hypothetical example spends $15 to make $20, with the possibility that 5% to 10% of buyers purchase a second product.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; the speakers discuss testing offers with paid ads but do not specify a startup budget.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: The speakers say products and offers could be tested quickly, including overnight, but do not give a time to first sale.

acquisition.how: Paid ads, marketplace listings and organic search can bring customers with software, but creative testing and spend decisions need human oversight.

onboarding.how: Digital checkout and automatic file delivery can onboard buyers without manual work.

delivery.how: A digital guide can be delivered automatically, while AI-assisted content creation and quality review still need human checks.

billing.how: An ecommerce checkout can collect payment and deliver digital products automatically.

support.how: Low-priced downloads may need limited support, but refund requests, access issues and product questions still need a process.

uk_applicability.notes: Digital guides can be sold to UK customers. Localize the content, comply with consumer and digital-content rules, and handle VAT appropriately.

risks: The speakers' margin and sales examples are hypothetical; no actual product economics are supplied.
A general store may have weak repeat purchasing when customers in different niches do not want each other's products.
Paid ads can lose money if conversion rates or customer acquisition costs are poor.
AI-generated guides need expert review, particularly for health, finance and safety topics.

delivery.how: AI can research and draft the plan, but source checking and quality assurance are needed before delivery.

tactics.name: Test the app through two paid traffic destinations
steps: Finish payment integrations and submit the app to the App Store.
Run one paid campaign to the landing page and another directly to the App Store.
Compare the conversion and cost results before choosing which route to scale.

tactics.name: Batch a month of niche video posts
steps: Search Instagram on desktop for a niche hashtag such as vegan recipes.
Use the Zapier browser extension to add selected video links to a spreadsheet.
Export the links as a CSV and use Apify to download the posts.
Route videos through Airtable and Zapier into a Bannerbear template that adds a recurring caption.
Send finished assets to Dropbox and bulk schedule them through Hopper HQ.
Review rights, attribution and output quality before publishing.

tactics.name: Use a recurring caption to convert viewers into followers
steps: Put a clear description of the page's niche at the top of each video.
Add a day-count or series hook to create a reason to visit the profile.
Place the caption before a key moment so viewers see it before they swipe away.
Track view-to-follow conversion by caption format.

tactics.name: Test guide offers and pricing from one store
steps: Use marketplace data, including Etsy searches, to identify guide topics people are already buying.
Create a small set of niche guides and list them in one Shopify store.
Run separate ad campaigns for different products, titles and positions.
Test price points across the discussed $17 to $99 range and keep the offer that performs best.
Track repeat purchases before assuming customers will buy across unrelated niches.

Describe the outcome in simple terms so prospects can assess the value quickly.

evidence_quality.rationale: Chris gives detailed first-hand descriptions of social content and workflow, and the guest explains how the content service works and sells. Several products are still ideas or pre-launch, the transcript has auto-caption errors, and many growth, pricing and conversion figures are estimates or hypotheticals.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris promotes his newsletter and podcast near the end of the transcript and refers to a course in the copyright discussion. No third-party sponsor read is evident.
